chunk_findings.detail: `baseline_for` captures `clock` before acquiring the lock and then reuses that same value for the post-lock `load` and for `_store`. In production `baseline_for_cfg` passes no `now`, so `clock` is the time at entry. If the suite lock is held for longer than `[baseline].keep` days, a waiting caller can use an expired baseline or store a measurement with a stale timestamp. For example, with `keep_days=1`, caller B enters at `t=0`, waits for the lock until `t=2 days`; if the store already has a complete entry with `measured_at=0`, B’s post-lock `load` uses `now=0`, sees age `0`, and returns the entry as fresh even though it is 2 days old. If there is no entry, B measures at `t=2 days` but `_store` writes `measured_at=0`, so the next caller at `t=2.1 days` treats it as expired and measures again, violating the “measure once per base sha” cache behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/baseline_store.py:baseline_for

chunk_findings.detail: Pruning is only called inside `if keep_days > 0`, so when `[baseline].keep` is 0 existing store entries are never pruned. Given a repo whose `.ddflow/local/baseline-store` contains old JSON entries from a prior non-zero keep, calling `baseline_for_cfg` with `keep=0` causes `load` to ignore them and `_store` to return a measured baseline without calling `prune`, leaving the old entries on disk. `prune(repo, 0, now)` would delete them, but it is not invoked, contrary to “0 keeps nothing” / pruning entries older than the configured keep.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/baseline_store.py:_store

chunk_findings.detail: The tests never exercise the stated “failure-text digest (path-normalised)” requirement. They only compare against `BS.digest_of("boom")`, a string containing no path. Given an implementation that returns a raw hash of the failure text, the same failure reported from two CI worktree paths such as `[REDACTED:path] ...` and `/var/tmp/ci/repo/tests/test_x.py:12: ...` would produce different digests, but every test in this file would still pass, violating the path-normalised digest requirement and the “store the failure digest, not only the id” intent.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_store.py:test_two_runs_on_one_sha_measure_the_base_once

chunk_findings.detail: This test does not actually prove that the measurement runs under the suite lock. The injected lock pre-stores a baseline before yielding, so the outer call finds the cache and skips measurement entirely. An implementation that acquires the lock, rechecks the cache, releases the lock, and then measures/stores outside the lock would pass this test and all other tests here, yet two concurrent processes seeing a missing sha could both measure after their lock windows, violating “A missing sha is measured once under the suite lock.”
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_baseline_store.py:test_the_measure_runs_under_the_lock_and_rechecks_after_it

chunk_findings.detail: `_store` persists `digest_of(text)` on raw `Measured.failures` values, and `digest_of` only truncates `content_digest` — it never path-normalises. `Measured` documents those values as failure text, and the only in-module caller never rewrites paths before hashing. Given a base failure `E AssertionError\n/wt/aaa/pkg.py:10: in test_foo` and the same failure under `/wt/bbb/pkg.py:10`, the stored digest differs, so a baseline red is treated as a new cause (the B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause case this store is supposed to close).

chunk_findings.detail: `baseline_for` captures `clock` before acquiring the lock and then reuses that same value for the post-lock `load`, the stored measurement timestamp, and `prune`. In production `baseline_for_cfg` passes no `now`, so `clock` is the time at entry. With `[baseline].keep=1`, caller B can enter at `t=0`, find no complete baseline, and wait on the suite lock until `t=2 days`; if another process stored a complete baseline at `t=0.5 days`, B’s post-lock `load` uses `now=0`, making `now - measured_at` negative and causing `_fresh` to accept a baseline that is already expired relative to the actual current time. If B instead measures after waiting, `_store` writes `measured_at=0` even though the measurement completed at `t=2 days`; a subsequent load at `t=2 days` sees the entry as older than the one-day keep and discards it, violating “measured once” and the keep-based pruning semantics.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/baseline_store.py:baseline_for

chunk_findings.detail: The optional prefixes in `_SCRATCH`, `_WORKTREE` and `_PYTEST` use `[^\s:'\"]*?`, which lets the match cross the same delimiters that `_END` treats as path boundaries (notably comma, right parenthesis and right bracket). As a result, a tree or pytest root later in the text can swallow an earlier path and its delimiter. For example, `normalise("/foo,/tmp/pytest-of-ci/pytest-1/test_x.py:1: boom")` matches from `/foo` through the pytest temp root and returns `<pytest-tmp>/test_x.py:1: boom`, erasing `/foo,`. Likewise `normalise("/foo,/tmp/ddflow-ci.abc/tests/test_x.py:1: boom")` returns `<tree>/tests/test_x.py:1: boom`. Since `digest` hashes this normalised text, failures that differ only in the non-temp path before the comma (e.g. `/foo` vs `/bar`) get the same digest, violating the stated “whole path components / keep everything after them” contract and potentially hiding a new cause.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/ci/failure_text.py:normalise

chunk_findings.detail: The lock tests still do not force the store write to happen before the lock is released. `test_the_measure_runs_while_the_lock_is_held` only records that the measurement callback sees `state["held"] == True`; it never checks that the JSON entry exists before the fake lock exits. `test_a_run_that_waited_for_the_lock_finds_what_the_holder_stored` also does not test the outer implementation's store timing because the injected lock pre-stores before yielding. An implementation that acquires the lock, checks the cache, measures, releases the lock, and then calls `_store` would pass both tests (the first sees the run under the lock; the second finds the pre-stored entry and never exercises the outer store), but with a real suite lock two processes could both miss the cache and measure: P1 measures and releases, P2 acquires before P1's store lands, sees missing, measures again. That violates “measured once under the suite lock”; the test should assert the store file is visible before the lock context releases, e.g. in the lock generator after `yield` but before clearing `held`.
